hyps.why: A skip directly into node 3 already provides an identity path, so upgrading edge 5 to a 3x3 conv adds less.
With a skip into the sink already present, an extra 1x1 conv on edge 4 is partly redundant.
With edge 0 removed node 1 carries no signal, so a conv on edge 2 has nothing to transform.
With edge 0 removed node 1 is dead, so a 3x3 conv on edge 4 contributes almost nothing.
Without edge 1, node 2 receives only a deeper, weaker signal via node 1, so the edge 5 conv has less to work with.
A strong conv path from input to output already exists, so another 3x3 on edge 5 has diminishing returns.
Replacing none with a conv restores a direct input-to-output path, a much larger gain than replacing any other op.
Replacing a removed edge with a 3x3 conv adds a whole new direct path, a larger gain than swapping one existing op for another.
Filling an empty edge with a 3x3 conv adds capacity and connectivity, more than replacing an existing op.
Adding a conv where the edge was empty gives a bigger gain than replacing an existing op.
